name: What is the difference between snaking and hydro-jetting for drain clogs?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between snaking and hydro-jetting for drain clogs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Snaking, also known as drain cabling, involves inserting a long, flexible auger into the drain to break apart or retrieve a blockage. It's effective for common clogs like hair or small obstructions. Hydro-jetting, on the other hand, uses a high-pressure stream of water to thoroughly clean the inside of pipes, removing stubborn blockages, grease buildup, and tree roots. Hydro-jetting is a more comprehensive cleaning method, often used for severe clogs or main sewer lines, while snaking is usually a first step for less complex issues. Both are tools CG Plumbing Solutions employs depending on the clog's nature.
acceptedAnswer.description: Snaking uses an auger to break up clogs, while hydro-jetting uses high-pressure water to clean pipes thoroughly. Hydro-jetting is for severe clogs, snaking for simpler ones.
